briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Operators Hold the Line on Tax as National Rescheduling and Psychedelics Momentum Build
briefs.top: Despite the 24% wholesale tax now a year old, Michigan dispensaries are holding steady on price and demand while lawmakers push a repeal and a new Ypsilanti store opens its doors. Nationally, DEA's rescheduling clock got a short pause but the bigger story is forward motion — a new Schedule III registration portal, Compass Pathways' psilocybin NDA on track for Q4, and a mega M&A bid reshaping the MSO landscape.

local.text: Michigan demand holds steady a year into the tax — Retail prices and consumer demand haven't collapsed under the 24% wholesale tax, with oversupply (not the levy) still the bigger price driver in Michigan's unlimited-license market.
Bloom City Club opens new Ypsilanti dispensary — The Ann Arbor-based chain is celebrating the launch with a slate of cannabis-themed events throughout October.
Senate Bill 810 keeps tax-repeal fight alive in Lansing — Sen. Jeff Irwin is co-sponsoring the repeal push even as he concedes it faces long odds against a $420 million road-funding hole.
Bay City turns cannabis tax dollars into shelter beds — Local officials are directing marijuana revenue toward housing support, a bright spot in an otherwise rough week for the industry.

Regulators clean house on bad actors statewide — State officials revoked 20 cultivation licenses and fined a company $2 million for shipping "dirt and mulch" labeled as marijuana, while also pulling Muha Meds' Ypsilanti license over a fake customer profile.

national.text: DEA rescheduling paused, not rejected — A judge stayed the Schedule III proceeding to weigh a new GAO report, with the government's response due October 13 and the underlying case still alive.
DEA opens new Schedule III registration portal — State-licensed medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs can now use the Form 225 process to register under the Controlled Substances Act.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin NDA stays on track for Q4 — The company holds a National Priority Voucher that could shrink FDA review to just 1-2 months for its treatment-resistant depression therapy COMP360.
Compass Pathways plants its flag in the U.S. — The psilocybin drugmaker cut the ribbon on its first U.S. office in Jersey City this week with local elected officials in attendance.
Curaleaf's $4-a-share Aurora bid reshapes MSO landscape — The proposed takeover represents a 45% premium and signals a new scale of cross-border cannabis consolidation.
